_provenance.notes: Steller sea lions (Eumetopias jubatus) were listed as Threatened under the ESA in 1990 and reclassified as Endangered (Western DPS) in 1997. Their decline in the 1970s-1990s coincided with pollock fishery expansion in the Bering Sea and Gulf of Alaska — the 'junk food' hypothesis. After extensive Section 7 consultations, NOAA implemented groundfish fishery restrictions including critical habitat protections, pollock A-season vessel caps, and no-trawl zones around major rookeries. The eastern DPS was delisted in 2013. The western DPS remains endangered with ~85,000 animals.
